beef.name: Beef

sections.whatItOffers: Cooked 90% lean ground beef is a dense source of vitamin B12 (about 99% of the reference in 3 ounces), zinc (about 67%) and iron (about 13%), with about 21 g of protein.
sections.howToEatIt: Brown for sauces, chilli and tacos, shape into burgers, or mix with grated vegetables or lentils to stretch it. Pair with vitamin C foods such as tomatoes or peppers.
sections.cycleRelevance: Iron needs are higher for women aged 19 to 50 (18 mg a day, against 8 mg for men), partly because of menstrual blood loss (NIH ODS). Iron from meat is absorbed more readily than iron from plant foods, so beef is an efficient source; 3 ounces provide about 2.4 mg.

source.usdaDescription: Beef, ground, 90% lean meat / 10% fat, patty, cooked, pan-broiled

cautions.text: Cook steaks, chops and roasts to 145 °F (62.8 °C) and let them rest for at least 3 minutes; cook ground meat to 160 °F (71.1 °C).
cautions.source: USDA FSIS, Safe Minimum Internal Temperature Chart (read 2026-10-27)

beef.evidence: Nutrient amounts and reference intakes only (USDA FoodData Central, NIH ODS).

tempeh.name: Tempeh

sections.whatItOffers: Tempeh is a firm, nutty cake of fermented whole soybeans. Half a cup gives about 17 g of protein, magnesium (about 22% of the reference), potassium and iron.
sections.howToEatIt: Slice or crumble and pan-fry, bake or grill with a marinade, or simmer into curries and chilli. Steaming it for a few minutes first mellows its flavour.
sections.cycleRelevance: Iron needs are higher for women aged 19 to 50 (18 mg a day, against 8 mg for men), partly because of menstrual blood loss (NIH ODS). Tempeh adds plant iron (about 2.2 mg in this serving), which is absorbed less readily than iron from meat; vitamin C in the same meal helps.

chicken.name: Chicken

sections.whatItOffers: Roasted skinless chicken breast is a lean, high-protein food: half a breast gives about 27 g of protein for about 142 calories, plus vitamin B12 and zinc.
sections.practicalServing: ½ breast, skinless (USDA: 0.5 breast, bone and skin removed = 86 g)
sections.howToEatIt: Roast, grill, poach or pan-fry, then slice into salads and wraps, shred into soups and bowls, or serve with vegetables and grains.
sections.cycleRelevance: No cycle-phase claim is made for chicken; it is mainly a lean protein source.

eggs.name: Eggs

sections.whatItOffers: A hard-boiled egg gives about 6 g of protein, vitamin B12, vitamin A and some vitamin D for about 78 calories.
sections.howToEatIt: Boil, poach, scramble or bake; slice into salads, grain bowls and sandwiches. Cook until the white and yolk are firm.
sections.cycleRelevance: No cycle-phase claim is made for eggs. A single egg supplies a modest share of most nutrients, and one of the few foods with some vitamin D.

tofu.name: Tofu

sections.whatItOffers: Firm tofu set with calcium sulfate is a plant protein with a lot of calcium: a quarter block gives about 14 g of protein and about 55% of the calcium reference, plus zinc and magnesium.
sections.howToEatIt: Press and cube for stir-fries and curries, crumble into scrambles, bake or pan-fry until golden, or blend silken types into sauces. It takes on the flavour of what it is cooked with.
sections.cycleRelevance: Calcium needs are 1,000 mg a day for women aged 19 to 50 (NIH ODS). Tofu made with calcium sulfate is one of the richer non-dairy sources; check the label, as tofu set with other coagulants has much less.

pork.name: Pork

sections.whatItOffers: Roasted lean pork loin gives about 24 g of protein, zinc (about 27% of the reference), vitamin B12 and potassium in 3 ounces, for about 178 calories.
sections.howToEatIt: Roast, grill or pan-sear, then slice thinly; it works with fruit, mustard and herbs, in stir-fries, or shredded into tacos.
sections.cycleRelevance: Iron needs are higher for women aged 19 to 50 (18 mg a day, against 8 mg for men), partly because of menstrual blood loss (NIH ODS). Lean loin is a modest source of iron (about 0.9 mg in this serving); other cuts and organ meats differ.

lamb.name: Lamb

sections.howToEatIt: Roast with garlic, rosemary and lemon, grill slices, or braise in stews and curries; rest the meat before carving.
sections.cycleRelevance: Iron needs are higher for women aged 19 to 50 (18 mg a day, against 8 mg for men), partly because of menstrual blood loss (NIH ODS). Lamb provides iron from meat (about 1.8 mg in this serving), absorbed more readily than iron from plants.

feta.name: Feta

sections.whatItOffers: Feta is a brined, tangy white cheese. An ounce gives calcium (about 14% of the reference), vitamin B12 and zinc for about 75 calories. It is salty.
sections.howToEatIt: Crumble over salads, roasted vegetables and eggs, bake with tomatoes, or serve with olives and bread.
sections.cycleRelevance: Calcium needs are 1,000 mg a day for women aged 19 to 50 (NIH ODS). An ounce of feta supplies about 140 mg, about 14% of that.

plain-yogurt.name: Plain yogurt

sections.whatItOffers: A 6-ounce container of plain whole-milk yogurt gives calcium (about 21% of the reference), vitamin B12, zinc and about 6 g of protein.

kefir.name: Kefir

sections.whatItOffers: A cup of low-fat plain kefir, a tangy drinkable fermented milk, gives calcium (about 32% of the reference), vitamin A, vitamin B12 and about 9 g of protein for 104 calories.
sections.howToEatIt: Drink cold on its own, blend into smoothies, pour over cereal or fruit, or use in place of buttermilk in baking and dressings.
sections.cycleRelevance: Calcium needs are 1,000 mg a day for women aged 19 to 50 (NIH ODS). A cup of kefir supplies about 316 mg, about 32% of that. No phase-specific claim is made for kefir.

miso.name: Miso

sections.whatItOffers: Miso is a salty, savoury fermented soybean paste. A tablespoon gives protein, fibre and a little zinc and iron for about 34 calories, mainly as flavour.
sections.howToEatIt: Whisk into hot (not boiling) water for soup, stir into dressings and marinades, or glaze vegetables and fish. A little goes a long way.
sections.cycleRelevance: No cycle-phase claim is made for miso. It is used in small amounts and is high in sodium (see the caution).
